title: Ezekiel Chapter 32 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 32 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 32 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 32.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 32, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word of the LORD came unto me
Take up a lamentation for Pharaoh
The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon thee
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came unto me
questions.explanation: This is stated in Ezekiel 32:1 where it says, 'And it came to pass in the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, in the first day of the month, that the word of the LORD came unto me, saying,'

questions.question: What is Pharaoh king of Egypt compared to in Ezekiel 32?
options: A young lion of the nations
questions.correctAnswer: A young lion of the nations
questions.explanation: This comparison is made in Ezekiel 32:2, where it says, 'Thou art like a young lion of the nations...'

questions.question: What will the Lord spread over Pharaoh according to Ezekiel 32?
questions.correctAnswer: A net
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:3 states, 'I will therefore spread out my net over thee...'

questions.question: Where will the Lord leave Pharaoh according to Ezekiel 32?
questions.correctAnswer: Upon the land
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:4 indicates, 'Then will I leave thee upon the land...'

questions.question: What will fill the valleys with Pharaoh's height according to Ezekiel 32?
questions.correctAnswer: Flesh
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:5 states, 'And I will lay thy flesh upon the mountains...'

questions.question: What will water the land where Pharaoh swims in Ezekiel 32?
questions.correctAnswer: Blood
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:6 mentions, 'I will also water with thy blood the land wherein thou swimmest...'

questions.question: What will the Lord cover when He puts Pharaoh out according to Ezekiel 32?
questions.correctAnswer: The heaven
questions.explanation: This is stated in Ezekiel 32:7, 'And when I shall put thee out, I will cover the heaven...'

questions.question: What will happen to the bright lights of heaven according to Ezekiel 32?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be made dark
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:8 says, 'All the bright lights of heaven will I make dark over thee...'

questions.question: What will the Lord do when He brings Pharaoh's destruction among the nations?
options: Vex the hearts of many people
questions.correctAnswer: Vex the hearts of many people
questions.explanation: This is found in Ezekiel 32:9, 'I will also vex the hearts of many people...'

questions.question: What will happen to the kings when they see Pharaoh's destruction?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be amazed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:10 states, 'Yea, I will make many people amazed at thee...'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 32, who will come upon Pharaoh?
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Babylon
questions.explanation: This is clearly stated in Ezekiel 32:11, 'For thus saith the Lord GOD; The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon thee.'

questions.question: The Lord will cover the heaven when He puts Pharaoh out. True or False?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is affirmed in Ezekiel 32:7, 'I will cover the heaven...'

questions.question: The rivers will be full of Pharaoh according to Ezekiel 32. True or False?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is stated in Ezekiel 32:6, 'the rivers shall be full of thee.'

questions.question: The text mentions Pharaoh being compared to a bear. True or False?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text compares Pharaoh to a young lion, not a bear, as seen in Ezekiel 32:2.

questions.question: The Lord will brandish His sword before the nations. True or False?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text specifically mentions the sword of the king of Babylon, not the Lord's sword, in Ezekiel 32:11.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 32 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 32 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 32:12, what will cause the multitude of Egypt to fall?
options: By the swords of the mighty
questions.correctAnswer: By the swords of the mighty
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:12 states, 'By the swords of the mighty will I cause thy multitude to fall...'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 32:13 promise will happen if the multitude of Egypt is destroyed as instructed in Ezekiel 32:12?
options: All the beasts from beside the great waters will be destroyed
The land will become fertile again
The people will be restored to their homeland
The sun will shine brighter on Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: All the beasts from beside the great waters will be destroyed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:13 says 'I will destroy also all the beasts thereof from beside the great waters;' following the destruction by the swords in verse 12.

questions.question: What imagery does Ezekiel 32:14 use to describe the condition of the waters after Egypt is made desolate?
options: Their rivers will run like oil
Their waters will dry up completely
Their rivers will flow with blood
questions.correctAnswer: Their rivers will run like oil
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:14 says, 'Then will I make their waters deep, and cause their rivers to run like oil.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 32:15 and 16, what will the desolation of Egypt cause the nations to do?
options: The daughters of the nations shall lament Egypt and all her multitude
The nations will rejoice over Egypt
The nations will ignore Egypt's fate
The nations will send armies to help Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The daughters of the nations shall lament Egypt and all her multitude
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:15-16 state that Egypt will be made desolate and the daughters of the nations shall lament for Egypt and her multitude.

questions.question: How can the destruction of Egypt in Ezekiel 32:15 teach Christians about the consequences of pride and disobedience?
options: God’s judgment serves as a warning to humble oneself and obey Him
Pride will always lead to wealth and power
God will protect the proud from destruction
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment serves as a warning to humble oneself and obey Him
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:15 shows that God will smite those who dwell in Egypt causing desolation, indicating consequences for disobedience and pride.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 32:18 instruct the prophet to do for the multitude of Egypt?
options: Wail for them and cast them down to the nether parts of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Wail for them and cast them down to the nether parts of the earth
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:18 commands, 'Son of man, wail for the multitude of Egypt, and cast them down... unto the nether parts of the earth.'

questions.question: In Ezekiel 32:19, what is said about Egypt's beauty compared to others in the nether parts of the earth?
options: Whom dost thou pass in beauty? go down, and be thou laid with the uncircumcised.
Egypt is less beautiful and shall be forgotten.
Egypt will shine above all nations forever.
Egypt’s beauty will be restored after destruction.
questions.correctAnswer: Whom dost thou pass in beauty? go down, and be thou laid with the uncircumcised.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:19 says Egypt is surpassed in beauty and must go down to be laid with the uncircumcised.

questions.question: What do Ezekiel 32:20 and 21 reveal about the fate of the mighty and the strong nations alongside Egypt?
options: They lie uncircumcised, slain by the sword in the midst of hell.
They will rise again after Egypt’s fall.
They will protect Egypt from destruction.
They prosper while Egypt is destroyed.
questions.correctAnswer: They lie uncircumcised, slain by the sword in the midst of hell.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:20-21 describe the strong among the mighty as fallen, uncircumcised, and slain by the sword.

questions.question: How should Christians view the imagery of destruction and lamentation in Ezekiel 32:16 in relation to prayer and intercession?
options: It encourages us to pray and lament over those who face judgment, seeking their repentance.
It teaches us to ignore the downfall of others.
It suggests we should rejoice over the destruction of others.
It shows that lamentation has no place in faith.
questions.correctAnswer: It encourages us to pray and lament over those who face judgment, seeking their repentance.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:16 shows lamentation for Egypt, which can inspire believers to intercede in prayer for others facing judgment.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase in Ezekiel 32:14 ‘cause their rivers to run like oil’ in practical spiritual terms?
options: It symbolizes a smooth but darkened condition, indicating judgment rather than blessing.
It means the rivers will bring healing and abundance.
It suggests the rivers will become clear and fresh.
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes a smooth but darkened condition, indicating judgment rather than blessing.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:14 uses 'rivers to run like oil' to depict a deep, slow, darkened river, symbolizing judgment on Egypt.

questions.question: What lesson about God’s sovereignty can be learned from Ezekiel 32:12-15 regarding the fate of nations?
options: God controls the rise and fall of nations according to His will and for His purposes.
Nations fall solely due to military strength.
Nations are independent of God's control.
Fate of nations is random and unpredictable.
questions.correctAnswer: God controls the rise and fall of nations according to His will and for His purposes.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:12-15 shows God declares He will cause Egypt’s multitude to fall and make the land desolate, demonstrating His sovereignty.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 32:15 emphasize the purpose behind God's judgment on Egypt?
options: So that they shall know that I am the LORD
So that Egypt will be forgotten forever
So that the people will become stronger
So that other nations will envy Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: So that they shall know that I am the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:15 concludes with God’s purpose in judgment: 'then shall they know that I am the LORD.'

questions.question: What does the presence of Asshur and his company in the grave, as mentioned in Ezekiel 32:22, indicate about the fate of powerful nations?
options: All powerful nations, like Asshur, will also face judgment and death.
Asshur will reign forever in power.
Asshur will escape judgment because of its might.
Asshur's fate is different from Egypt's.
questions.correctAnswer: All powerful nations, like Asshur, will also face judgment and death.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:22 describes Asshur and all her company as slain and fallen by the sword, indicating judgment on powerful nations.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 32:18 commands the prophet to rejoice for the multitude of Egypt and their allies.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:18 commands to 'wail for the multitude of Egypt,' not to rejoice.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 32:12 states that the multitude of Egypt will be destroyed by the swords of the mighty nations.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:12 clearly states the multitude will fall by the swords of the mighty.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 32 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 32.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 32:23, what is described as being set in the sides of the pit?
questions.correctAnswer: Whose graves
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:23 states, 'Whose graves are set in the sides of the pit,' referring to the graves of those slain.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 32:24, what is said about Elam and all her multitude?
options: All of them slain, fallen by the sword
They are rulers over the nations
questions.correctAnswer: All of them slain, fallen by the sword
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:24 states, 'There is Elam and all her multitude round about her grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 32:25, how are the graves of the multitude described?
options: All of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword
questions.correctAnswer: All of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:25 says, 'her graves are round about him: all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword.'

questions.question: Which peoples are mentioned in Ezekiel 32:26 as having their graves round about him?
options: Meshech, Tubal, and all her multitude
questions.correctAnswer: Meshech, Tubal, and all her multitude
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:26 names 'Meshech, Tubal, and all her multitude' with graves round about him.

questions.question: Ezekiel 32:27 states that the mighty fallen of the uncircumcised have laid what under their heads?
questions.correctAnswer: Their swords
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:27 says, 'they have laid their swords under their heads,' referring to weapons of war.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 32:31, who shall be comforted over all his multitude slain by the sword?
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:31 states, 'Pharaoh shall see them, and shall be comforted over all his multitude, even Pharaoh and all his army slain by the sword.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'nether parts' (Ezekiel 32:24) most accurately mean?
questions.correctAnswer: The underworld or lowest regions
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 32:24, 'nether parts' (Hebrew: תַּחְתִּיּוֹת) refers to the underworld or the lowest parts of the earth where the dead reside.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Ezekiel 32:23-32 to depict the fallen nations?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:23-32 employs parallelism by repeating similar phrases describing different nations lying slain and uncircumcised, a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of fallen mighty and judgment as seen in Ezekiel 32:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 19:21
questions.explanation: Revelation 19:21 describes the defeat of the beast and kings by the sword of the Lord, echoing the judgment and fall of mighty warriors as in Ezekiel 32:27.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with the lamentation over Egypt’s fall in Ezekiel 32:16?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 46:10
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 46:10 laments the fall of Egypt, similar to Ezekiel 32:16 where daughters of nations lament Egypt’s multitude.

questions.question: What event is described immediately before the lamentation in Ezekiel 32:18?
options: The word of the LORD coming to Ezekiel in the twelfth year, fifteenth day
The calling of Ezekiel as a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD coming to Ezekiel in the twelfth year, fifteenth day
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:17 precedes verse 18 and states, 'It came to pass also in the twelfth year, in the fifteenth day of the month, that the word of the LORD came unto me.'

questions.question: What is the significance of the repeated mention of 'uncircumcised' in Ezekiel 32:24-30 in its cultural and theological context?
options: It signifies being outside the covenant community of Israel
It indicates a higher spiritual status
It refers to people who are priests
It denotes those who are righteous
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies being outside the covenant community of Israel
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 32:24-30, 'uncircumcised' refers to Gentile nations outside the covenant of Israel, symbolizing separation from God's chosen people and judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 32:7-8 use cosmic imagery to describe the judgment upon Egypt?
options: By darkening the sun, moon, and stars
By flooding the land with water
questions.correctAnswer: By darkening the sun, moon, and stars
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:7-8 says God will 'cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light,' symbolizing cosmic judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 32:32 states that Pharaoh and all his multitude will be laid in the midst of the circumcised with them that are slain by the sword.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:32 states Pharaoh will be laid 'in the midst of the uncircumcised with them that are slain by the sword,' not the circumcised.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 32:11 predicts the sword of the king of Babylon will come upon Pharaoh.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:11 explicitly states, 'The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon thee,' referring to Pharaoh.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 32 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 32 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 32:15 teach about God's nature in relation to judgment?
options: God's nature is hidden in times of crisis
God's judgment is arbitrary and unjust
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals Himself through judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:15 states, 'then shall they know that I am the LORD,' indicating that God's judgment serves as a revelation of His identity and holiness.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine sovereignty is taught in Ezekiel 32:11 regarding the fate of Egypt?
options: God sovereignly uses foreign powers to execute judgment
God is powerless against worldly kings
Human kings control their own destiny apart from God
God allows evil to triumph over His purposes
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly uses foreign powers to execute judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:11 says, 'The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon thee,' showing that God uses Babylon as an instrument of His sovereign judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human sinfulness is emphasized in Ezekiel 32:27 regarding the slain uncircumcised?
options: Sin results in separation from God's covenant people
Sin grants eternal life despite transgressions
All humans are automatically part of God's covenant
Sin has no consequence for those outside Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Sin results in separation from God's covenant people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:27 describes the uncircumcised fallen in hell, highlighting separation from God's covenant community due to sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 32:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:7 describes God covering the heavens and darkening the stars, sun, and moon, demonstrating His all-powerful control over creation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is underscored in Ezekiel 32:9 when God says He will vex the hearts of many people?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:9 shows God actively bringing destruction and vexation as a just response to sin and rebellion.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 32:2-6 prepare the theme of divine judgment and desolation found in later prophetic literature?
options: By portraying Egypt's downfall as both cosmic and comprehensive
By focusing solely on Egypt's political alliances
By ignoring God’s role in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: By portraying Egypt's downfall as both cosmic and comprehensive
questions.explanation: Verses 2-6 use imagery of rivers, mountains, and blood to foreshadow total and universal judgment, a theme developed in later prophets.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Ezekiel 32:16-32 make by listing the nations in the nether parts of the earth?
options: It shows the universal scope of God's judgment against proud nations
It promises all nations ultimate salvation
It denies the reality of death and judgment
It focuses only on Israel's enemies without broader implications
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the universal scope of God's judgment against proud nations
questions.explanation: The lamentation over Egypt and other nations in the underworld emphasizes God's sovereign judgment extending beyond Israel to all nations.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 32:4 and Ezekiel 32:5 teach about God's judgment?
options: God's judgment results in both physical destruction and total exposure
God's judgment is hidden and secretive
God's judgment only affects spiritual realms
God's judgment is partial and limited to individuals
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment results in both physical destruction and total exposure
questions.explanation: Verse 4 speaks of corpses exposed to birds and beasts, and verse 5 speaks of flesh laid upon mountains, indicating comprehensive physical devastation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 32:22 and Ezekiel 32:24 teach about the fate of the nations opposed to God?
options: God's judgment leads to death without honor among the uncircumcised
God spares the mighty nations from destruction
God grants eternal life to all nations regardless of sin
God's judgment is symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment leads to death without honor among the uncircumcised
questions.explanation: Both verses describe nations like Asshur and Elam lying slain, uncircumcised, bearing shame in the grave, showing dishonorable judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 32:28 and Ezekiel 32:31 teach about Pharaoh's end?
options: Pharaoh's fall is total and he is consigned to the company of the dead
Pharaoh will be victorious and exalted in the afterlife
Pharaoh's death is insignificant in God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh's fall is total and he is consigned to the company of the dead
questions.explanation: Verse 28 states Pharaoh will be broken among the uncircumcised dead, and verse 31 says he will be comforted over his slain multitude, confirming total defeat.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Ezekiel 32:11-12 contradicts divine justice by punishing whole nations. What does Ezekiel 32:11-12 actually teach?
options: God uses nations as instruments of judgment for their own sins
God punishes only individuals, not nations
God is indifferent to the fate of nations
questions.correctAnswer: God uses nations as instruments of judgment for their own sins
questions.explanation: Verses 11-12 describe Babylon's sword coming on Egypt to destroy its multitude because of their sin, demonstrating just and purposeful divine judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught in Ezekiel 32:13 about God's judgment on creation?
options: God's judgment affects both humans and animals
God's judgment spares animals from destruction
God's judgment is exclusively punitive to humans
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment affects both humans and animals
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 32:13 says God will destroy all the beasts from beside the great waters, showing judgment extends beyond just humans.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 32:14 specifically demonstrate in God's judgment?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: God's power to make waters deep and rivers run like oil in verse 14 shows His sovereign control over nature in executing judgment.

questions.question: What theological synthesis emerges from Ezekiel 32:16 and Ezekiel 32:18 about the fate of the nations in eschatology?
options: Nations experience a collective lamentation and descent to Sheol
Nations are ultimately redeemed and exalted
Nations remain indifferent to divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Nations experience a collective lamentation and descent to Sheol
questions.explanation: Verse 16 speaks of lamentation over Egypt, and verse 18 describes the multitude cast down to the nether parts of the earth, illustrating collective judgment and mourning.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 32:3 illustrate God's attribute of covenant faithfulness despite judgment?
options: God fulfills His promises to punish the arrogant
God abandons His covenant in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God fulfills His promises to punish the arrogant
questions.explanation: Verse 3 shows God spreading a net over Pharaoh, fulfilling His covenantal justice by punishing those who defy Him.
